ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and counterparties against the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 sanctions registers, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN list, UK OFSI consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Interpol Red Notices, and domestic law-enforcement PEP databases; full PEP status determination with Enhanced Due Diligence under AML/CFT Act 2009 sections 15 and 22, the FMA AML/CFT Supervision Manual, and the Companies Office 'know your customer' compliance expectations for reporting entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online portal — 'New Zealand Companies Register' (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or te reo Maori; if a foreign script is used, a romanized transliteration must be supplied in the application; names may include Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and limited punctuation; the statutory suffix 'Limited' or approved abbreviation 'Ltd' is mandatory for a limited liability company; the name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing registered name or reserved name on the Register; Maori words and official geographic names are checked against iwi consultation and historical-name protocols.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of receiving a name rejection notice from the New Zealand Companies Office, the applicant or its registered agent may file a formal reconsideration request through the Companies Office online portal; the reconsideration must set out the statutory grounds of non-conflict and non-objectionability under sections 20–22 of the Companies Act 1993, include the original name reservation reference, evidence of any consent or authorization, and be signed by the applicant or authorized agent; if the office maintains the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand. If the Registrar later determines that the name was improperly registered, the company will be required to change its name under section 23.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally acceptable for companies that do not conduct day-to-day management from the registered address, provided a physical New Zealand street address (not a post-office box) is lodged with the Companies Office and the address can accept legal service of process. For the specified digital advertising and media-buying activity, the Inland Revenue Department may disregard a virtual office for tax-residence substance analysis if the company is managed-and-controlled from a foreign low-tax jurisdiction; regulated financial institutions and correspondent banks (including Mercury and Wise) may reject a purely virtual office model for a 'medium risk enhanced' AML/CFT customer. A commercial serviced office or business hub in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (estimated 35–45% probability of an unannounced physical inspection or documented-compliance audit within the first two years). AML/CFT supervisors (Department of Internal Affairs) and the New Zealand Companies Office may conduct on-site verification of registered office address and business substance, particularly where the board is non-resident and turnover is high relative to staff/office presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), primarily sections 5 (incorporation), 10 (constitution), 19 (certificate of incorporation), 22 (name restrictions), 24 (name reservation), 33-35 (share allotment and capital), 42 (registered office), 88 (share register), 122-123 (registered office and address for service), 124 (first directors), 151 (director consent), and 210 (annual return). Also relevant: Financial Reporting Act 2013, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ngā Tari Kōmihana o Aotearoa), a division of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: New Zealand Companies Office — Online Incorporation Application (Registration of a Company) pursuant to the Companies Act 1993, Form 1 (Incorporation of a Company) as embedded in the electronic registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under New Zealand law. Shares may be issued as nil-paid, partly paid, or fully paid as determined by the board, and there is no escrow deposit requirement. For an International Company using a New Zealand corporate trustee or nominee structure, the shareholder capital is fixed by the constitution and board resolution; the company must only maintain a registered office in New Zealand and a resident agent. Banking partners may internally require an initial deposit, but that is not a Companies Act requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY] LIMITED (the "Company")

Adopted by the directors of the Company on [Date] at [Time] at the Company's registered office at [Address], New Zealand.

RESOLVED:
1. CONSTITUTION AND NAME: The Constitution filed with the New Zealand Companies Office upon incorporation is hereby adopted in full and the Company's name is confirmed as [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY] LIMITED (Company No. [number]).

2. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: The initial share capital of the Company is established at NZ$[amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares of NZ$[par value] each. The allotment and issue of such shares to the initial subscribers is approved, and the directors are authorized to receive subscription monies, issue share certificates, and complete all entries in the share register.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND RESIDENT AGENT: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [physical street address], New Zealand, and the Company approves the appointment of [name of licensed resident agent], a resident agent within the meaning of section 122 of the Companies Act 1993, to act as the Company's address-for-service in New Zealand.

4. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS: The following persons are appointed as the first directors of the Company: [Full Name] (Managing Director), [Full Name] (Creative and Media Director), and [Full Name] (Finance Director). Each director has consented to act and satisfies the eligibility criteria under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993. The board is authorized to file all necessary consents with the Companies Office.

5. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: [Full Name] is appointed as Company Secretary, and [Full Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each with delegated authority for banking, regulatory, and operational matters consistent with these resolutions.

6. BANK ACCOUNTS AND PAYMENT RAILS: The Company shall open corporate bank and payment accounts, including Mercury ACH, wire transfer facilities, and Wise, with signatory authorities as follows: any one director jointly with the Chief Financial Officer, or two directors jointly, in accordance with the approved banking mandate.

7. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND COMPLIANCE: The Board adopts the corporate governance pack tabled at this meeting, including the conflicts-of-interest register, delegated authority limits, and AML/CFT risk procedures. The directors are authorized to register the Company with Inland Revenue (IRD number and GST if applicable), and to make any necessary filings under the Financial Service Providers Act if the Company’s activities are determined to constitute financial services.

8. COMMERCIAL AUTHORITY: The managing director is delegated authority to execute contracts for digital advertising media arbitrage and affiliate lead generation (ISIC 7310) up to NZ$[amount] per contract, above which board approval is required.

This Resolution is executed as a written resolution and is to be recorded in the Company's minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, online name reservation service (via www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for the proposed company name (e.g., "[International Company] Limited"). Provide up to five alternative names in order of preference, confirm that the proposed name complies with section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, and pay the application fee (including the NZ$10 name reservation fee) online. The name is assessed for availability and if available, the applicant shall obtain a name reservation number valid for 20 working days. If the name includes restricted words (e.g., "bank", "insurance", "trust"), provide the required consent from the relevant supervising authority.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (online form)
Identification document of the applicant (passport or national identity card)
Name availability search result
If restricted word included: written consent from the relevant NZ authority (e.g., Reserve Bank, FMA, or MBIE)
In case of a foreign company name: certificate of good standing or proof of foreign registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation with revised names or request a review under section 22(4) of the Companies Act, providing evidence of distinctiveness or consent from the prior holder. Alternatively, incorporate under another reserved name and later apply for a name change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Incorporation Submission to the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the online incorporation application on the Companies Office portal. Provide the following: the reserved company name and reservation number; the proposed constitution (either the standard model form in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act or a custom constitution); the principal place of business and registered office address in New Zealand; the address for service; the names, dates of birth, residential addresses, and passports/licenses of all initial directors; the full names and share allocations of initial shareholders; and a declaration that the company is being incorporated for a lawful purpose outside any prohibited business. The applicant must also sign a statutory declaration confirming compliance with the Companies Act. Upon submission, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation under section 19, confirming the incorporation date, company number, and name.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application (Form 1 equivalent)
Company Constitution (custom or notice that Schedule 1 model form is adopted)
Written consent to act as director from each director (sections 151-152 Companies Act)
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement, title or letter from the premise owner)
Identity documents for each director and shareholder
Name reservation number/certificate
Declaration of compliance and lawful purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application (for example, incomplete director consents or an invalid registered office address), the applicant or agent must respond within 10 working days via the online portal, providing the corrected documents. If the Registrar issues a formal refusal, the applicant can re-submit the application after correcting defects or appeal to the High Court under Part 24 of the Companies Act by filing a judicial review application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Resident Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; professional incorporation and nominee service providers licensed under the Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure that the company's registered office is at an actual physical address in New Zealand (not a PO Box). The registered office must be staffed for at least 20 hours per week if shared with other customers of the service provider. If the company has no New Zealand resident director, appoint a licensed resident agent using Form 8 (Notice of Change of Registered Office and/or Appointment of Resident Agent). The agent must sign a formal acceptance. File the Form 8 online
required_dossiers: Form 8 (Notice of Change of Registered Office / Resident Agent Appointment)
Acknowledgment from the resident agent (signed)
Proof of registered office physical address (lease, utility bill, title or service provider agreement)
Copy of the certificate of incorporation
Consent of any director or secretary whose address is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office rejects the registered office address (e.g., it is a mailbox), obtain a compliant street address and re-file Form 8. If the resident agent resigns, the company must appoint a replacement within 5 working days; otherwise, the Registrar may initiate strike-off proceedings under section 340.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Issuance of Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the company; registered office minutes recorded and kept in corporate records; no filing with Companies Office required unless allotment details need to be recorded (not separately filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or pass a written resolution under section 91 of the Companies Act) to adopt the pro forma first board resolution set out above. Determine the share consideration, whether full prepayment is required or whether the shares are to be issued as unpaid/partly-paid, and issue share certificates. Record all allotments in the share register. The register must be available at the registered office. For a nominee/trust structure, ensure that the trustee or nominee signs the relevant declarations and that the beneficial ownership is separately recorded in a trust register or internal records to satisfy AML due diligence with banks.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting, or written resolution
Share application forms from each initial shareholder
Board resolution authorizing share allotment
Central/company share register
Payment receipts or escrow confirmation for subscription monies
Certificates issued to shareholders after allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any share issuance is defective (e.g., directors signed without valid appointment), cure by ratifying the allotment in a subsequent board meeting and, if necessary, refund and re-issue shares. If a share certificate is rejected by a financial institution for lack of countersignature, re-execute the certificate with the required signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD) via the Business Registration portal; New Zealand Companies Office (for NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company is automatically issued a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and should apply for an IRD number online through the Business Registration portal. Complete 'Form IRD 484A (Non-Resident Company)' if the company is a non-resident company; otherwise file the appropriate company tax registration. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 if expected taxable supplies in New Zealand exceed NZ$60,000 per annum; otherwise, voluntary registration can be made. Register as an employer for PAYE if employees are engaged. For a tax-exempt international company structure, coordinate with the tax advisor to file the appropriate foreign-company status and ensure that no unintended permanent establishment arises.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation
Irm date and company tax details (IRD 484A if non-resident)
Application for GST registration (or declaration of threshold exemption)
Bank account details of the company
Contact details of registered agent and directors
In case of employee: employer registration (PAYE) application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is delayed or the company receives a compliance notice for non-registration, submit the overdue IRD number application with an explanation of delay. If GST is registered late, apply for penalty remission under the Tax Administration Act 1994, providing grounds of reasonable excuse (e.g., reliance on professional advice).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Documentation and AML/CFT Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for AML/CFT if the entity is a reporting entity; otherwise, private-sector banking KYC and Companies Act governance record-keeping standards.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a comprehensive corporate governance pack, including: a board charter, directors' conflicts-of-interest policy, delegation authority schedule, minutes for the first board meeting, and an annual compliance calendar. Maintain shareholders' register and directors' interest register under the Companies Act. Prepare an AML/CFT compliance manual and KYC files for all beneficial owners, directors and signatories (including passports, proof of residential address, source of funds). Even if the affiliate media-buying business is determined not to be a financial service, all banks will require full KYC documentation. If the company provides any financial services (e.g., holding funds on behalf of affiliates in a structured manner), apply to register as a financial service provider on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and become an AML/CFT reporting entity. Update the Companies Office within 10 working days of any director or shareholder changes.
required_dossiers: Corporate governance manual and first board minutes
Register of shareholders and register of directors' interests
AML/KYC file (beneficial owners' identification, proof of address, source of funds)
Policy on staggered or multi-tier board approvals for media buying
If applicable: Financial Service Provider registration application
Annual return and corporate calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA issues an AML/CFT remediation notice, immediately appoint an anti-money laundering compliance officer and an external auditor to perform a gap analysis, submit a remedial action plan within 20 working days, and correct any filing on the FSPR. If the Companies Office sends a compliance inquiry, respond with the updated register and minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Rail Integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand registered commercial banks (ANZ, BNZ, Westpac, ASB) or non-resident friendly payment fintech providers (Mercury, Wise; international wire networks); all subject to AML/CFT obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a corporate bank account with the selected institution. Submit the certificate of incorporation, constitution, name reservation certificate (if incorporated recently), directors and shareholders KYC, first board resolution opening the account and appointing signatories, proof of registered office, and business plan describing the media-buying and affiliate lead generation model, anticipated transaction volumes, counterparty types, and source of revenue. The bank will perform an AML/CFT risk assessment, treat the business as Medium-Risk Enhanced, and may require additional documentation, such as a source-of-funds declaration, a trust deed (if the shareholder is a trust), or business references. Once opened, integrate Mercury ACH, wire transfer, and Wise by adding the bank account as a connected funding source and completing the fintech providers' separate KYB (Know Your Business) verification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Constitution and adoption minutes
First board resolution for banking and signatories
Passport and proof of address of directors/UBOs
Proof of registered office and resident agent appointment
Detailed business plan and revenue model
AML/KYC self-certification form from the bank
Financial statements or opening balance sheet (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initial application is declined, identify the specific concerns (financial crime risk, jurisdictional risk, lack of local substance) and either: (a) apply to a different bank with better non-resident onboarding, (b) appoint a New Zealand resident director with corporate experience to reduce substance risk, or (c) engage the registered agent's company management arm to co-sign the account. If the bank requires an in-person interview, conduct it at the registered agent's office or via video conference in accordance with the bank's permitted procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription to Annual Statutory Compliance and Reporting Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; Inland Revenue; Financial Markets Authority (if applicable); all enforced through the electronic register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish an annual compliance calendar. File the company's annual return with the Companies Office every year (Form AR) within 20 working days of the anniversary of incorporation, containing director and shareholder details and payment of the annual fee. If the company qualifies as a small company (i.e., not a large company under the Financial Reporting Act 2013), no audited financial statements are required; nonetheless, maintain accounting records sufficient for the IRD. Prepare and file income tax returns and GST returns as applicable. For any change to directors, shareholders, registered office, or address for service, file the corresponding Form 5, Form 6, or Form 8 within 10 working days of such change. Conduct an annual director review of AML risk and update KYC files for any new directors or beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Annual return (AR) online filing confirmation
Financial statements or adequate accounting records
TAX filings and IRD confirmation
Updated share register and directors' register
Board resolutions approving annual report
Bank account statements for continuance reviews
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company misses the annual return deadline, file it immediately online, pay the late filing fee, and if the company is struck off, apply for restoration under section 329 of the Companies Act (within 20 years; before that, within 3 years with no formal fee if none). For tax penalties, apply for remission in writing to IRD. If the Registrar removes the resident agent for breach, appoint another agent and file the updated Form 8.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE) — Business Registration and Support; Commerce Commission (Fair Trading) for advertising practice oversight; Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) for voluntary self-regulation of advertisements and affiliate disclosures; Department of Internal Affairs for unsolicited electronic messages enforcement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is mandated for pure digital advertising agency services, affiliate lead generation, or media buying under ISIC 7310. If the company chooses to establish a physical office in New Zealand, it requires a simple Business Zoning Certificate / Certificate of Occupancy from the local territorial authority under the Building Act 2004. For email-marketing services, the company must be listed as a marketing operator with the Department of Internal Affairs (if notifying subscribers via electronic messages), and comply with the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and local territorial authorities (resource consents under the Resource Management Act 1991)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA. Digital media buying and affiliate lead generation are not listed on the mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment schedules. No discharge permit, resource consent, or EIA approval is required. If the company were to operate large server racks on-site, a low-impact building certificate might be required under local council rules but still not an EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The operation is digital and produces no point-source wastewater, VOCs, or atmospheric emissions. If the company occupies an office: comply with local council noise limits, and ensure any HVAC and electronic equipment meets the Energy Efficiency Regulations; if any standby generator is installed, the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality must be considered; all digital waste (batteries, electronics) must be handled in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and e-waste stewardship guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance is not required for a purely digital company without staffed premises. If the company leases an office: (i) obtain a Fire Safety Certificate / Landlord's Fire Statement under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; (ii) install and maintain smoke detection and a Means of Escape compliance schedule (Building Act 2004, Code Clause C); (iii) if employees work in premises, develop a Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 worker engagement plan, conduct a hazard risk assessment for office/computer use, and maintain first aid kits. If only using a registered agent's shared office, the agent's certificate covers physical clearance, but the company must document its own health and safety policy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (IR) – New Zealand's national tax authority; online portal: myIR (https://myir.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without a physical NZ presence must register for an IRD number (TIN) through the Non-Resident Company Registration process on the Inland Revenue website. The entity must file application IR596 ('Registration of an IRD number for a non-resident company') with certified company incorporation documents, a certificate of good standing, and a New Zealand agent/resident director appointment (unless an exemption applies). Upon approval, the entity receives an IRD number and, if taxable supplies are expected above the GST registration threshold, must simultaneously register for GST via Form GST1.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory election mechanisms include: the Look-Through Company (LTC) election under Subpart HB for qualifying closely held NZ companies; the elective GST margin scheme for land transactions under Subpart 8C of the GST Act 1985; and hybrid mismatch elections/treatment alignments under Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007. A non-resident company can also elect to be treated as a fully-fledged NZ tax resident if central management and control is exercised in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period (past or prospective turnover)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping mandate applies. E-invoicing is voluntary but supports PEPPOL interoperability; businesses may issue compliant GST tax invoices with prescribed particulars. GST returns and payments are filed via Inland Revenue's myIR or approved gateway services, but there is no pre-clearance requirement for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported by the supplier within 28 days of supply, with the supplier retaining documentary evidence of export. Services are zero-rated under section 11A(1)(k) of the GST Act 1985 when supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not physically performed in New Zealand and are not directly connected with land, moveable property, or persons located in New Zealand. Electronically supplied remote services to overseas B2B customers are zero-rated; B2C remote services supplied to New Zealand residents by non-resident suppliers remain subject to GST where the NZ threshold is met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Trade Single Window entry / Customs CUS830)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or other bank payment/transfer evidence
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract
Packing list and weight certificate (where applicable)
Proof of physical exportation (e.g., carrier receipt, port turnaround evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims and require the exporter to establish, on the balance of probabilities, that the supply was genuinely exported or supplied to a non-resident outside New Zealand. Fraudulent zero-rating claims constitute tax evasion under the Tax Administration Act 1994, attracting a shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall, criminal prosecution, and imprisonment. Civil penalties include: 10% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for gross carelessness, and 40% for an abusive tax position, plus use-of-money interest. Clawback provisions require the supplier to reverse input tax credits and pay the unremitted GST plus penalties if the zero-rating conditions are retrospectively not satisfied, and the Commissioner may reassess returns within the statutory time bar.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), the central bank of New Zealand and the monetary authority for the New Zealand dollar, is the senior bank regulator in the Realm of New Zealand. In the Cook Islands, the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) is the statutory licensing and prudential supervision authority for banks, foreign exchange dealers, trustees, and international companies, while the New Zealand dollar remains the operational settlement currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully open current and capital account with no general exchange-control approval gate, no restrictions on foreign-currency accounts, no surrender obligations, and no conversion quotas. A Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) operating in the Tax_Exempt_Zone may freely hold and remit NZD, USD, AUD, EUR, and GBP. The principal practical remittance hurdle is not exchange control but tax characterisation: if the CK_IC generates New Zealand-source income, dividends, royalties, or interest paid to non-residents may be subject to New Zealand non-resident withholding tax at 15% or a lower applicable treaty rate, and the transaction must be supported by transfer-pricing documentation. Pure offshore affiliate media-buying income retained in the international-company treasury is not subject to New Zealand tax if the company has no New Zealand permanent establishment and does not carry on a taxable New Zealand activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for affiliate media-buying or other service export receipts in New Zealand or the Cook Islands. A CK_IC may retain foreign currency indefinitely in multi-currency accounts. The only compliance margin is AML/CFT and financial-intelligence reporting: beneficiary banks may require underlying publisher contracts, ad-network statements, and invoices to establish the commercial source of each cross-border receipt, and deposits above internal risk thresholds may be subject to enhanced source-of-funds review before they are available for outward disbursement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium and conditional. Offshore digital EMIs are viable only as auxiliary settlement rails, not as the primary treasury or capital-escrow bank. Wise Business is operationally feasible for NZD, USD, EUR, and GBP disbursements to affiliate networks and publishers. Mercury is generally unavailable to a Cook Islands International Company structure. New Zealand does not operate an EMI licensing regime; non-bank payment providers must register on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register and join an approved dispute-resolution scheme, and any provider serving the Cook Islands entity should hold a relevant FSC money-service or payment-service permission. Legal constraint: an offshore EMI is not a licensed deposit-taker and cannot hold client escrow, cannot provide a New Zealand bank sort code for local BECS settlement, and must never be used as the sole receiving bank for inbound capital injections. The final structure should maintain a FSC-licensed domestic bank account as the treasury core and use EMIs only for high-speed low-value affiliate payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a CK_IC, remote-only bank opening is generally not permitted. At least one natural-person director and the ultimate beneficial owner, if different, must be introduced through an FSC-licensed trustee, licensed agent, or commercial bank; the initial KYC interview is typically physical, or alternatively a notarially verified video interview witnessed by a licensed New Zealand or Cook Islands professional. For purely New Zealand bank accounts, online onboarding may be accepted for domestic low-risk customers, but a tax-exempt offshore international company is classified as higher risk, so in-person or notarised identity verification and a board-authorisation pack are effectively mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore international-company structure flagged as tax-exempt, nominee-managed, or with non-resident directors and no local economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation of the Cook Islands International Company; FSC licence or registered-agent certificate; constitutional documents and trust deed, if applicable; current certificate of incumbency; register of directors and shareholders; substance narrative and physical office or licensed agent arrangement; source-of-wealth explanation for each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC_7310 affiliate media buying and performance-marketing treasury showing high-volume cross-border payments to unregulated publishers, networks, and affiliate payees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed advertiser agreements; publisher and affiliate-network contracts; valid insertion orders; sample invoices from publishers; server-side click and impression logs; reconciliation reports from ad platforms; wire statements traceable to each campaign; monthly cash-flow projection and media-buying budget.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a foreign jurisdiction where the bank cannot establish the source of funds or the commercial purpose of the transfer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six to twelve months of source-account bank statements; executed share-subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board resolution approving the capital injection; share register reflecting issuance; tax residence certificate of the lending shareholder; FSC-approved business-plan reference; signed source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to counterparties in high-risk, sanctioned, or tax-secrecy jurisdictions disproportionate to the affiliate-media business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor due-diligence file containing the legal name, country, beneficial owner, and sanctions screening of each payee; underlying contracts and tax identification numbers; evidence that the payee is a real operating publisher; ad harvester or traffic logs supporting the payment amount; declaration that no payee is a prohibited person or sanctioned jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on offshore digital EMIs or fintech wallets as the sole banking channel, creating an unregulated shadow treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Primary relationship with a FSC-licensed commercial bank; funds-flow matrix demonstrating that the EMI is used only as a pass-through payout rail; written compliance opinion confirming EMI registration or licensing; copies of the EMI's KYC profile; monthly reconciliation between banking ledger and EMI ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route for inbound capital is a SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's bank to the CK_IC capital-escrow account maintained at ANZ Bank (Cook Islands) Limited or Bank of Cook Islands Limited. Wire narrative must clearly read SHAREHOLDER CAPITAL INJECTION / SHARE SUBSCRIBER CONTRIBUTION, reference the CK_IC registration number, and identify the ultimate transferor. The beneficiary bank should be instructed to classify the payment as foreign direct investment equity capital or other investment loan, as applicable, for New Zealand balance-of-payments and international-transaction reporting. Verification pack: board resolution approving the injection, executed subscription or loan agreement, share register with the issuance entry, source-of-funds evidence, FSC acknowledgement for the IC structure, and certified identities of the transferor and beneficial owner. No prior exchange-control approval is required in New Zealand or for an international company's offshore capital receipts; however, funds may be held for one to three business days pending enhanced due-diligence clearance where the amount exceeds the bank's risk threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Affiliate-media and lead-generation trade settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for international publisher payouts, New Zealand BECS for domestic NZ media sellers, SEPA Credit Transfer for European publishers, and US ACH through a permitted partner bank or Wise Business for United States affiliate payees. MT202 cover payments may be used where interbank liquidity routing requires a separate cover message. Commercial letters of credit in MT700 format are not a natural payment rail for digital media arbitrage because there is no physical shipment; a standby letter of credit or bank-issued purchase-order guarantee is preferred only where an advertiser or publisher requires bank protection. All outbound wires must carry a purpose code matching the underlying media-buying service, a reference to the publisher contract, and an invoice or statement of account. Settlement instruction must be verified independently against the publisher's authorised banking details to prevent invoice-redirection fraud.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards up to 12 months with a licensed New Zealand or FSC-supervised bank, available for hedging committed USD, AUD, EUR, or GBP affiliate-media cash flows into NZD.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with no onshore settlement or restricted convertibility, permitted only where the CK_IC has an underlying commercial obligation and an executed ISDA or FX master agreement with an approved bank.

Cross-currency swaps for converting long-dated foreign-currency media-purchase liabilities into NZD and aligning period-end profit repatriation, subject to board approval and coverage of actual commercial exposure.
Vanilla FX options for downside protection on large campaign prepayments, with no leveraged, exotic, or speculative structures permitted beyond documented media-buying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR) — section 208, Companies Act 1993, with simultaneous NZBN details confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 working days after the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation or a date fixed by the Registrar; due annually on a recurring calendar basis.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$200 (approx. USD 124) under section 209, Companies Act 1993; continued default triggers Registrar's default notice and administrative strike-off of the company from the Companies Register under section 318; directors may face personal liability for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Significant Persons (UBO) annual confirmation — filed as an integrated component of the Annual Return (sections 206C and 206H, Companies Act 1993)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE — beneficial ownership module of the Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Annual Return, within 10 working days after each return date; any shareholding transfer that changes beneficial ownership or control of 25% or more must be notified within 10 working days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company liable to a fine of up to NZ$10,000 (approx. USD 6,200) and each responsible director or officer liable to a fine of up to NZ$5,000 (approx. USD 3,100) for failure to maintain, update, or accurately confirm the beneficial ownership register; knowingly false confirmation carries additional criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements (mandatory only if the company qualifies as 'large') filed with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Delivered to the Companies Register together with the Annual Return, within 10 working days after the annual return date; preparation and audit must be completed against the company's balance date, typically 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under section 44, Financial Reporting Act 2013 — fine up to NZ$10,000 for the company and up to NZ$20,000 per director; repeated non-filing may support Registrar strike-off action and director disqualification proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IRD annual nil tax return / tax-exempt status declaration confirming no New Zealand-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, filing due by 7 July of the following income year; for a substituted balance date, due within six to seven months after that balance date; a nil return annually confirms the tax-exempt offshore status of the International Company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 (approx. USD 155), escalating incremental penalties for continued default, and shortfall interest at the IRD prescribed rate on any assessed liability; persistent default may trigger default assessments and IRD debt-enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, a New Zealand company must prepare and file audited financial statements in any year where it qualifies as 'large', meaning it meets at least two of the following three thresholds: (a) total assets exceeding NZ$5.5 million (approx. USD 3.4 million); (b) annual revenue exceeding NZ$10 million (approx. USD 6.2 million); (c) 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees. An audit may additionally be required at shareholders' requisition holding 25% or more of voting rights.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit entities must apply NZ IFRS issued by the New Zealand Accounting Standards Board (Tier 1); Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS with the Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); non-publicly-accountable small and medium entities may apply the NZ Small and Medium-Sized Entities Accounting Standards (Tier 3 and Tier 4) instead of full NZ IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the company must confirm its current significant persons (UBOs) with the Registrar as part of the Annual Return. Any shareholding transfer or change resulting in beneficial ownership or control of 25% or more of shares or voting rights must be recorded and notified within 10 working days of the change. The annual confirmation certifies that the Register of Significant Persons is complete, accurate, and up to date; breach constitutes an offence carrying fines against the company of up to NZ$10,000 and against each responsible officer of up to NZ$5,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Significant Persons (Beneficial Ownership Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 500 per annum (NZD 400 – 800) inclusive of registered office address provision and statutory compliance agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,700 – 12,400 per engagement (NZD 7,500 – 20,000) for a typical small-to-mid-size performance media buying entity; a reduced review engagement fee applies where statutory audit thresholds are not triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not provide general tax holidays. The R&D tax credit is 15% of eligible R&D expenditure, with a 26.5% cash-out rate for loss-making companies. Non-resident companies are taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment or on specific statutory income. No preferential headline rate applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 (Company Tax Return) filed electronically via the Inland Revenue (IRD) myIR portal or through an approved tax agent. Non-resident companies with only New Zealand-sourced income may file Form IR4 or IR4NZ as directed by IRD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th day of the month following the balance date, or by 7 July for a standard 31 March balance date. Extended deadlines apply for tax agents, typically to the following 31 March or 31 July depending on terminal tax dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and IRD number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name of the Cook Islands International Company and its New Zealand IRD number. Non-residents must obtain an IRD number before filing.
Disclose non-resident status and state whether the company carries on business through a fixed establishment or PE in New Zealand. This determines the scope of assessable income.

Report only income sourced in New Zealand, including income from a PE, dividends, interest, or royalties sourced in New Zealand. Foreign-sourced income is excluded. Provide a breakdown of income categories.

Claim only expenses directly attributable to the New Zealand PE or New Zealand-sourced taxable income. Apportion shared group expenses and ensure transfer pricing adjustments are reflected per New Zealand TP rules.

Offset deductible expenses against New Zealand-sourced income. Losses from a New Zealand PE may be carried forward if the same PE continues, but the carryforward is limited to 5 years for tax purposes.

Calculate tax at 28% on taxable income. Claim credits for non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) deducted at source, foreign tax credits, and any RWT credits. Do not claim imputation credits unless a New Zealand-resident shareholder, which is not the case for a Cook Islands IC.
If a New Zealand tax agent represents the company, provide the agent's name and tax agent number. IRD accepts electronic filing through agents with appropriate authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 immediately, with a further NZ$250 if the return remains outstanding 30 days after the due date. Late payment penalties are 1% of unpaid tax on the due date, then an additional 4% after 7 days. Use-of-money interest applies daily at the prescribed underpayment rate (8.35% as of September 2024). Civil shortfall penalties range from 20% to 150% of the tax shortfall depending on the type of breach.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident company. If fully imputed, the dividend may be exempt (0%) under the imputation credit mechanism. However, a Cook Islands International Company is not a New Zealand tax resident; dividends it pays to its shareholders are not subject to New Zealand NRWT unless sourced in New Zealand. Branch profits remitted from a New Zealand PE to a Cook Islands IC are not subject to dividend withholding tax, but the branch profits are taxed in New Zealand at the corporate rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: New Zealand does not have a double tax agreement with the Cook Islands. Therefore, no DTA relief is available. To invoke treaty relief under any other treaty, the company must submit Form IR103 (NRWT rate entitlement certificate), provide a foreign tax authority-issued Certificate of Residence, and provide supporting declarations to the IRD. For Cook Islands ICs, statutory NRWT rates apply without reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties is 15%; on interest it is 15%, unless the 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) is used for qualifying eligible securities. No DTA protection for Cook Islands ICs, so the 15% statutory rate applies to royalties and interest unless the AIL is validly applied to interest payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is mandatory where cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$10 million annually. The IR4 must disclose related-party dealings exceeding NZ$1 million. Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of NZ$1.14 billion or more. Cook Islands International Companies are subject to Cook Islands confidentiality and annual return rules, but New Zealand TP thresholds apply to New Zealand-source operations.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand applies the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007. There are no OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the IRD may recharacterise entities lacking commercial substance. A Cook Islands IC must have real functions, assets, and risks in the Cook Islands; otherwise, New Zealand may attribute its income to a New Zealand resident. The Cook Islands International Companies Act prohibits the carrying on of business within the Cook Islands and requires annual returns. International tax substance doctrines apply in cross-border audits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to file New Zealand tax returns, underreporting New Zealand-sourced media buying income, creating fictitious invoices from the Cook Islands IC to shift profits, or knowingly providing false information to the IRD to defeat tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, imprisonment for up to 5 years for evading tax. Civil shortfall penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall. Late payment penalties and use-of-money interest apply. Criminal fines may also be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under section 133 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 for the company's tax debts if they knowingly assisted in evasion. Courts can order civil restitution, asset freezing, travel bans, and disqualification from managing companies. Imprisonment is possible for fraudulent conduct. The corporate veil is pierced for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (GAAR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Cook Islands IC as a pure conduit without real staff, offices, business decision-making, or risk management; earning affiliate commissions or royalties without substantive functions, assets, or risks; presenting a tax avoidance purpose as dominant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may apply the GAAR to reconstruct the arrangement and attribute income to a New Zealand resident. Shortfall penalties of 20% (unacceptable tax position) or 100% (abusive tax position) apply. Interest and late payment penalties follow. In the Cook Islands, carrying on business in the Cook Islands could result in loss of exempt status and penalties under the International Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign tax returns knowing the position is abusive face civil penalties equal to up to 100% of the tax shortfall. They may be personally liable for the company's tax debt under the Companies Act 1993 provisions for reckless trading or fraudulent conduct. Travel bans and asset freezing orders can be issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the affiliate media buying entity to move funds via Mercury ACH, wire transfer, or Wise without performing customer due diligence; failing to file suspicious transaction reports; structuring transactions to avoid AML thresholds; processing proceeds from fraud or undeclared principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (NZ), financial institutions and reporting entities face civil penalties up to NZ$2 million per breach and criminal penalties for individuals including imprisonment up to 2 years. The Cook Islands AML/CFT Act 2018 imposes fines and imprisonment for money laundering, and failure to report suspicious transactions carries separate penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally prosecuted if they knowingly authorise money laundering. Penalties include imprisonment, significant fines, travel bans, asset freezes, and forfeiture. Directors may be disqualified and held personally liable for civil penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZ$10 million; paying non-arm's length affiliate commissions (e.g., excessive margin to the CK IC); failing to disclose related-party transactions in the IR4 when they exceed NZ$1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: No separate TP penalty, but shortfall penalties apply: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for unacceptable position, and 150% for evasion. IRD may adjust income and impose use-of-money interest. Record-keeping failures may attract fines up to NZ$25,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for penalties if they sign returns without reasonable care in respect of transfer pricing. In fraudulent circumstances, personal liability for the company's tax shortfall and civil restitution may be imposed.
